The graph of the linear function $g$ is shown, where $y = g(x)$. What is the y-intercept of the graph of $g$?
explanation: Choice D is correct. The y-intercept of a graph is the point where the graph intersects the y-axis. The graph of function $g$ shown intersects the y-axis at the point $(0, 10)$. Therefore, the y-intercept of the graph of $g$ is $(0, 10)$.
